name: SalesTarget.ai
summary: All-in-one B2B outbound platform: a lead database of 840M+ professional profiles with credit-based enrichment, cold email with unlimited inboxes and warm-up, LinkedIn automation, and a built-in CRM and dialer, sold as separate modules or one bundle per team.
best_for: small sales teams and agencies that want a B2B lead database, cold email with unlimited inboxes and warm-up, LinkedIn automation and a basic CRM under one login, priced per organisation with 3 seats included rather than per seat
skip_if: you need independent proof of data quality before you buy, because we found no third-party reviews we could read; or your plan is AI-personalised email at volume, because SalesTarget's own AI costs 5 email credits per email; or you need LinkedIn volume from day one, because a standard account takes 42 days of warm-up to reach 20 connection requests a day
honest_knock:
The credit numbers on the plan cards shrink once you read the help centre's price list. Unlocking an email address costs 2 credits, a phone number 5, intent data 3, and adding a lead to a list costs another credit. Growth's 2,000 credits are therefore about 660 leads a month with a verified email, or about 250 if you also want the phone number. Sending is billed the same way on a separate balance: a plain email costs 1 email credit, but an AI-personalised email written by SalesTarget's own AI costs 5, so Growth's 5,000 emails become 1,000 if every step is AI-written. Connecting your own LLM key brings that down to 2. None of this is hidden, but none of it is on the pricing page either.

The 'Super Saver' badge on the bundle is hard to check. Lead Explorer Launch ($49, 2,000 credits) plus Email Outreach Growth ($30, 5,000 emails) comes to $79 for the same allowances as the $169 All In One Growth plan. The $90 difference buys one LinkedIn automation slot and Copilot, and the LinkedIn tab showed no stand-alone price when we read it on 1 October 2026, so we cannot tell you whether the bundle actually saves money. The yearly toggle has the same problem: it says 5%, and the real discount runs from 0% to about 15% depending on the module.

Two documents disagree on how to leave. The pricing FAQ says you can cancel any time from the dashboard with no cancellation fee, while the terms say subscriptions auto-renew unless 30 days' notice is given and that partial terms are not refunded. Cancel well before the renewal date and keep a record. The 'Labor Day Sale, Limited Time Only' banner still running on 1 October is a small thing, but it is the first thing on every page. The LinkedIn side is cautious by design: the help centre starts a standard LinkedIn account at 3 connection requests a day, takes 42 days to reach 20 a day, caps it at 100 a week, and halves your daily limit if fewer than 30% of requests are accepted. We found no independent reviews we could read: there is no Product Hunt listing, and G2 and Trustpilot blocked our reader. We have not used the product.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-01 on salestarget.ai/pricing, tab by tab, and in the help centre at help.salestarget.ai) Sold either as one bundle or module by module, priced per organisation rather than per seat; the help centre says every plan includes 3 team seats. All In One, the default tab with a 'Super Saver' badge: Growth $169 a month (1 LinkedIn automation, 5,000 emails a month, 2,000 enrichment credits), Scale $319 (2 LinkedIn automations, 100,000 emails, 4,000 credits), Ultimate $679 (3 LinkedIn automations, 500,000 emails, 6,000 credits, plus a $300 wallet credit), Enterprise on request; yearly $1,926, $3,636 and $7,740. Lead Explorer on its own: Launch Credit $49 for 2,000 credits a month, Builder Credit $99 for 4,000, Expansion Credit $169 for 6,000; yearly $588, $1,188 and $1,788. Email Outreach on its own: Growth $30 for 5,000 emails a month, Hypergrowth $85 for 100,000, Light Speed $345 for 500,000 with a $200 wallet credit; yearly $306, $867 and $3,519. CRM & Dialer: Growth CRM $40 a month plus $20 per added user, and a Dialer Bundle at $29 a month with one local number and 400 credits, extra credits at $0.025, extra numbers $3 local or $5 toll-free. The LinkedIn tab showed no plans when we read it, and a 'Customize Yourself' tab builds a plan from sliders. The toggle says yearly saves 5%, but the actual saving we calculated ranges from none (Lead Explorer Launch and Builder, the dialer) to about 15% (Email Outreach, the CRM). The wallet credits can only be spent on domains bought inside SalesTarget, not on email accounts, and are non-refundable. Free trial: the pricing FAQ says 50 credits and no credit card; the homepage adds '7-day trial'. A banner reading 'LABOR DAY SALE ... Limited Time Only!' was still on every page on 1 October. Payment is by credit card. Salestarget LLC, with an address in Wilmington, Delaware.

compare_with.name: Apollo
compare_with.why: Apollo is the obvious alternative: like SalesTarget it puts a B2B contact database, enrichment and email sequences in one product. The difference is how you pay. Apollo charges per seat: on our reading of 11 September 2026 it had a free plan with 900 credits per seat per year, and paid plans of $49, $79 and $119 per seat a month on annual billing, or $65, $99 and $149 month to month, with Organization requiring three seats. SalesTarget, read on 1 October 2026, charges per organisation with 3 seats included: All In One Growth at $169 a month covers the whole team, where three Apollo Professional seats paid monthly come to $297. That makes SalesTarget cheaper on paper for a small team. Apollo has the free plan, which SalesTarget does not, and a large base of users and reviews you can check before you buy, which we could not find for SalesTarget. Pick Apollo if you want the established option and are one or two people; consider SalesTarget if you are a team of three that also wants LinkedIn automation and a dialer in the same bill.
